summary.prose: When a raw writer changes the content of a head that already has history, the head ends one revision past its log and the lifecycle service refuses to approve, review or complete it. The service now recognises that state when it checks integrity: if the head's own hash holds and its content differs from the last logged revision, it logs the head's revision as an update by the system actor, marked as an adopted raw write, in the same queue slot, and then runs the operation. A hand-edited revision number, a hash mismatch and a log ahead of the head are still refused. No writer changes.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Keep the artifact log in step with raw content writes (ISSUE-7e0f65fc1a518722): a content change a raw writer (writeArtifact kind 'content') makes to a head that has history must leave the log in step with the head, so LifecycleService approves, reviews and completes the new revision.

api.name: LifecycleService.apply
api.signature: apply(id: string, op: Operation, by: Actor, detail?: TransitionDetail, ctx?: EvidenceContext): Promise<ApplyResult>

parameters.name: id
parameters.purpose: The artifact whose lifecycle operation is applied

parameters.name: op
parameters.purpose: For approve, review and complete the integrity of the head against its log is checked first

parameters.name: by
parameters.purpose: The actor of the operation; an adopted entry is by the system actor, not by this one

errors.condition: thrown with reason hash-mismatch, log-ahead-of-head, or head-ahead-of-log when the head's content hash equals the last logged revision's (a changed number alone); nothing is written or logged

preconditions: For approve, review and complete the head has its own hash intact (checkHeadIntegrity is ok)
postconditions: When the head was ahead of the log with changed content, the log ends with an 'update' entry for the head's revision and hash by insrc:system, with outcome result 'adopted', appended before the operation's own entry and under the same per-artifact queue slot
After the adoption the integrity check passes and the operation proceeds as for any head in step
A head in step, an unlogged head and every refusal leave the log exactly as before (no entry is added)

api.name: checkIntegrity
api.signature: checkIntegrity(a: ContentView, log: ChangeLogEntry | readonly ChangeLogEntry[] | undefined): Integrity

parameters.name: a
parameters.purpose: The head's description, payload and lifecycle

parameters.name: log
parameters.purpose: The log, or the entry to compare with

returns.meaning: Unchanged: it still answers head-ahead-of-log for a head later than the log; the decision to adopt is the caller's

postconditions: Unchanged for every input; the service calls it again with the adopted entry appended

api.name: History.appendLog
preconditions: The caller holds the artifact's queue, so no store write interleaves
postconditions: The entry is the last revision-bearing entry of the log

dataModelChanges.details: A new use of the existing entry shape, no new field: operation 'update', actor insrc:system (kind system), revision {number, contentHash} copied from the head, outcome {result: 'adopted', summary: 'a content change written outside the store was logged when the head was approved, reviewed or completed'}, no status change. The entry's timestamp is the time of the adoption, not the time of the raw write. It is appended only when the head is later than the last revision-bearing entry, its stored hash matches its own content, and its content hash differs from that entry's.

dataModelChanges.entity: Integrity rule for approve, review and complete
dataModelChanges.details: head-ahead-of-log is no longer final for a head with changed content and an intact hash: the service logs it and re-checks. It stays final for a head whose number is ahead but whose content hash equals the last logged one, and hash-mismatch and log-ahead-of-head are unchanged. The check function itself does not change.

errorCases.scenario: The revision number of a head was edited by hand and its content did not change
errorCases.detection: In LifecycleService.apply the head's content hash equals the content hash of the last revision-bearing log entry while its number is higher (checkIntegrity answers head-ahead-of-log)
errorCases.response: LifecycleConflictError head-ahead-of-log as before; nothing is written or logged
errorCases.userImpact: A person has to resolve it; the head is not approved

errorCases.scenario: The body of a head was edited by hand without recomputing the stored hash
errorCases.detection: checkHeadIntegrity: the stored contentHash differs from the hash of the head's own content
errorCases.response: LifecycleConflictError hash-mismatch before any adoption is considered; nothing is written or logged
errorCases.userImpact: A person has to resolve it

errorCases.scenario: The log is ahead of the head (a merge brought in a later revision)
errorCases.detection: checkIntegrity: the head's revision number is below the last logged one
errorCases.response: LifecycleConflictError log-ahead-of-head as before; no adoption

errorCases.scenario: The adopted entry cannot be appended (the sidecar write fails, or the entry is malformed)
errorCases.detection: History.appendLog throws inside the store.updateAndLog callback
errorCases.response: The error is thrown out of apply; the head is not written and the operation is not applied; the log keeps whatever the failed append left (an append is one record)
errorCases.userImpact: The operation fails and can be retried; the next attempt finds the head still ahead of the log and adopts again

errorCases.scenario: A raw writer changes the head again between the adoption and the operation
errorCases.detection: None needed: adoption and the operation run under the artifact's one queue slot in store.updateAndLog, and a raw write that lands before or after is seen by the next call as a head ahead of the log again
errorCases.response: The later raw write is adopted by the next approve, review or complete; the operation that ran judged the content it read
errorCases.userImpact: A draft changed after a review is not covered by it: the revision moves, so the review is stale

edgeCases.input: A head with no revision-bearing log entry (never approved or reviewed)
edgeCases.expected: No history, so checkIntegrity passes and nothing is adopted or logged, as before

edgeCases.input: Two raw content writes in a row on a head with history (revisions 2 and 3, log at 1)
edgeCases.expected: One adopted entry at revision 3 and its hash; revision 2 is not logged, and the integrity check passes afterwards

edgeCases.input: A raw write changes the content and a second raw write restores the logged content, so the head is at revision 3 with the revision-1 hash
edgeCases.expected: The content hash equals the last logged one, so it is not adopted and head-ahead-of-log is refused; a person resolves it

edgeCases.input: A head is approved after adoption
edgeCases.expected: The log ends with the adopted update at the head's revision followed by the approve at the same revision; the next integrity check finds head and log equal

edgeCases.input: A complete on a unit whose members are checked
edgeCases.expected: Each member is checked the same way where the service checks it (lifecycle-service.ts line 260 path); a member with a raw write is adopted under its own queue slot, or refused for the other reasons

edgeCases.input: apply of an operation that is not approve, review or complete
edgeCases.expected: No integrity check, so no adoption; such operations run as before

invariantsToPreserve.text: A head whose stored hash does not match its content is never approved, reviewed or completed (hash-mismatch is refused before any adoption)
A log ahead of the head (log-ahead-of-head) is refused
A refused operation writes nothing and logs nothing
A head with no revision-bearing log entry is approved normally
A content change by a raw writer still returns the head to draft and keeps its Signoff entries; nothing in storage.ts changes
ArtifactStore.write still tolerates head-ahead-of-log on an ordinary write and refuses the other integrity reasons

migration.stateBefore: A raw content write (writeArtifact kind content, src/workflow/storage.ts) on a head that already has a revision-bearing log entry moves the head one revision past its log; checkIntegrity (src/workflow/artifact-core/lifecycle.ts) answers head-ahead-of-log and LifecycleService.apply (src/workflow/artifact-core/lifecycle-service.ts) refuses to approve, review or complete it and writes nothing, as reproduced on 2026-11-02. ArtifactStore.write tolerates the state on an ordinary write (src/workflow/artifact-core/store.ts).
migration.stateAfter: LifecycleService.apply, for approve, review and complete, first logs a head that is ahead of its log with intact hash and changed content as an update by insrc:system with outcome adopted, in the same queue slot, and then applies the operation as for a head in step. The refusals for a hand-edited number, a hash mismatch and a log ahead of the head are unchanged. No writer and no stored head changes.

migrationSteps.action: Add the adoption step to LifecycleService.apply before the integrity refusal: when checkIntegrity answers head-ahead-of-log, the head's own hash holds and its content hash differs from the last revision-bearing entry, append the adopted update through the store's history and check again
Add the tests: a raw write on a head with history approved, reviewed and completed; the refusals that must stay; the failing append; the daemon approve path

Record the decision and the limit (the adopted entry carries the time and actor of the adoption) in docs/plans/core-data-model.md item 3 and docs/plans/team-workflow.md, and update the write inventory note of the raw content writers

migration.backwardCompat: No stored data changes and no API signature changes. A head that was refused before with head-ahead-of-log and a real content change is now approved, reviewed or completed; that is the fix. Heads already stuck in that state are adopted the next time they are approved, reviewed or completed, with an adopted entry dated at that time. A log with adopted entries is read by the same code, since the entry uses the existing update operation and outcome fields.

alternativesConsidered.name: The service adopts a raw content write when it judges integrity
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: LifecycleService.apply, finding a head ahead of its log whose own hash holds and whose content differs from the last logged revision, first logs that revision as an update by a system actor, then runs the operation.
alternativesConsidered.approach: In LifecycleService.apply, inside the store.updateAndLog callback that already runs checkIntegrity for approve, review and complete, a head-ahead-of-log result is no longer final. When the head's stored hash matches its own content (checkHeadIntegrity is ok) and the head's content hash differs from the content hash of the last revision-bearing log entry, the head is a raw content write that was never logged: the service appends an 'update' entry at the head's revision, hash and time, by the system actor, with an outcome saying a raw write was adopted, in the same queue slot, and then checks the operation as before. A head whose number is ahead but whose content hash equals the logged one (a hand edit of the number), a hash-mismatch and a log-ahead-of-head stay refused. No writer changes.
pros: One place, no change to the many synchronous writers, and every present and future raw writer is covered
The history gains the missing entry, so the log is in step afterwards and later checks pass without a special case
Keeps the refusal for a hand-edited number, a hash mismatch and a log ahead of the head
cons: The entry is written at the next lifecycle operation, not at the time of the write, so the log's timestamp and actor for that revision are the adopter's
The service decides that an unlogged content change is legitimate; it cannot tell a raw writer from someone who edited the body and recomputed the hash

alternativesConsidered.name: Move every raw content writer onto the store
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Replace writeArtifact kind 'content' at each caller with ArtifactStore.write, which logs the revision as it writes.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Each raw content writer (synthesize, the workflow rpc, the gates, resolve-comment, the tracker unit head, the two build ledger writers) obtains the repository's ArtifactStore and calls its async write with an actor, so the head and the log move together under the store's queue and journal. writeArtifact keeps only the meta-only kind. The callers that are synchronous become async.
pros: The log is written at the time of the change with the real actor
One rule for every write: the store; the integrity states cannot arise from a content write
cons: Many call sites in different modules become async, with their tests; callers that run without a daemon (library use, tests) have no store to call
The store takes a repository registry entry and a sidecar the library code does not have; a large change for a defect with one visible symptom
Writers that run before any lifecycle operation (build ledger, unit head) gain history they never needed
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: The log is exact, but it changes many synchronous callers and needs a store where there is none; a large change across modules for one symptom.

alternativesConsidered.name: writeArtifact appends the log entry itself
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: writeArtifact, after a content write that mints a revision on a head with history, appends a revision-bearing entry to the sidecar from the path.
alternativesConsidered.approach: writeArtifact derives the repository root and the sidecar from the artifact path and appends an 'update' entry for the new revision through a synchronous variant of the history append, so no caller changes.
pros: No caller changes; the log is written at the time of the write
cons: It bypasses the store's queue and journal, so a raw write racing a store operation can interleave and reintroduce an integrity conflict
writeArtifact has no actor and no repository registry; the path-to-sidecar rule would be a second copy of the registry's
The history API is asynchronous; a synchronous append is a new surface
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Bypasses the store's queue and journal and needs a synchronous history surface; it risks creating the opposite conflict.

alternativesConsidered.name: Raw writers call an adopt step after writing
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A new ArtifactStore method logs the head's current revision as an update; each raw content writer that runs where a store exists calls it after writeArtifact.
alternativesConsidered.approach: ArtifactStore gains an adopt(id, actor) that, under the queue, appends an 'update' entry for the head's current revision when the head is ahead of the log with its own hash intact. The daemon-side raw writers (synthesize, the workflow rpc, resolve-comment) call it right after writeArtifact; the library-only writers are left, which still leaves them able to produce the state.
pros: The entry is written at the time of the change by the writer's own actor
No change in the integrity rules
cons: Every daemon writer must remember to call it, and a new one that forgets reproduces the defect
Writers without a store (gates, the build ledger) are not covered, so the defect stays reachable
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Better timing than a1 but depends on every writer remembering a call, and leaves the library writers uncovered.
